title: Calculated fields and items, slicers and timelines

videos.script: Lesson 10 built pivot tables that add things up. This lesson makes them answer more, and makes them easier to steer. {{field}} First, arithmetic inside the pivot. Divide revenue by bags and you get what a bag of coffee really sold for. Multiply price by bags in the same place, and the total comes out more than ninety times too big. Both come from one rule. A calculated field works on totals, never on rows. {{sums}} Then the calculated item, which adds a row of its own and quietly counts the same money twice. You will see why to avoid it, and what to use instead. {{item}} Then the controls. A slicer is a filter drawn as buttons. Click Wholesale, and every number in the pivot is wholesale. A timeline does the same for dates, a month or a quarter at a time. {{slicer}} One slicer can drive two pivot tables at once, when they share the same source. {{connections}} And last, the formula Excel writes when you click a pivot cell. It finds a number by its name, not its position. When a slicer moves the rows, it still finds the right one, or it tells you plainly that it cannot. {{getpivotdata}}
